title: Maternal Cardiac Arrest
sources: Critical Vector — OB Pocket Guide: Maternal Cardiac Arrest (BAACC TO LIFE)
AHA Obstetric Life Support (OBLS) 2024; AHA ACLS 2025 refresh

changelog.change: Initial entry — the BAACC TO LIFE differential, CPR modifications for pregnancy (manual LUD, IV above the diaphragm, remove fetal monitors), and resuscitative cesarean delivery timing.

summary: Two patients — manage the MOTHER first; do not monitor or resuscitate the fetus during the arrest, and remove the fetal monitors. From 20 weeks (fundus at/above the umbilicus): continuous manual left uterine displacement, IV/IO access ABOVE the diaphragm, and prepare for a resuscitative cesarean delivery to be done AT the arrest site within 4–5 minutes.

items: B — Bleeding / haemorrhage (PPH, abruption, uterine rupture)
A — Anaesthesia complications (high spinal, local-anaesthetic systemic toxicity)
A — Acute cardiopulmonary (PE, MI, cardiomyopathy, ARDS, amniotic fluid embolism)
C — Cardiac arrhythmia / electrolyte (hyperkalaemia, DKA, hypokalaemia)
T — Trauma / toxins / overdose (magnesium toxicity, opioids)
O — Other obstetric (amniotic fluid embolism, uterine inversion, sepsis)
L — Labelling (check every reproductive-age female for pregnancy)
F — Fever / sepsis (Group A Strep — can kill in 2–8 h)

body.text: CPR modifications (≥ 20 wk or fundus at/above the umbilicus)

rows: CONTINUOUS, do not stop. From the patient's RIGHT: push the uterus left and up. From the LEFT: pull the uterus left and up. Start as soon as the fundus is at/above the umbilicus. Do NOT use lateral tilt / wedging — that's obsolete. The gravid uterus cuts venous return 25–30%.
Same hand placement (lower half of the sternum), rate 100–120/min, depth ≥ 2 in. Large / dense breasts: rotate the hand slightly toward the patient's shoulder, heel perpendicular to the sternum.
ALWAYS above the diaphragm — aortocaval compression makes below-diaphragm access unreliable. IO: proximal humerus preferred.
Anterolateral or anteroposterior pads — NOT on breast tissue. Remove fetal monitors before the shock (theoretical arcing). Energy doses unchanged.
Standard ACLS doses — do NOT alter or withhold epinephrine or amiodarone. 100% O2 via BVM. If on a magnesium infusion: stop it and give calcium gluconate 1 g IV.
Only to confirm pregnancy (femur length ≥ 30 mm or BPD ≥ 45 mm ≈ ≥ 20 wk), NOT fetal heartbeat. Must not impede CPR or extend a pulse check beyond 10 s.

body.text: If there is no ROSC by ~4 minutes of a witnessed maternal arrest with a fundus at/above the umbilicus, START the RCD so delivery is complete by ~5 minutes. Do it AT the arrest site — do NOT transport to an OR. RCD relieves aortocaval compression → autotransfusion of ~500 mL → > 50% chance of maternal ROSC; it is a maternal resuscitation manoeuvre first, a fetal one second. Continue CPR throughout. Vertical skin + uterine incision is fastest; minimal instruments; skip prep.

Postpartum arrest and amniotic fluid embolism: consider AFE with sudden cardiovascular collapse + hypoxia + DIC in labour or immediately postpartum — supportive resuscitation, aggressive DIC correction (the 'A-OK' regimen — atropine, ondansetron, ketorolac — is described but unproven), early ECMO. Group A Strep sepsis in the peripartum period is fulminant — broad-spectrum antibiotics + clindamycin within the hour.
